title: Average cost at a query node
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be finite sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and suppose there is a finite Fourier basis for functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$ and contains the constant-one function. For an available coordinate $i$ and a family of decision trees $T_v$ indexed by $v\in\Omega$, with each $T_v$ using only the other available coordinates, the tree that queries $i$ and then follows $T_{x_i}$ has auxiliary average cost $1+\mathbb{E}_{v\sim\pi}[\text{auxiliary average cost of }T_v]$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
A finite nonempty index set with decidable equality indexes a real basis of functions on $\Omega$
The distinguished basis vector is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
The queried coordinate belongs to the available coordinates
Each child tree is defined on the available coordinates with the queried coordinate removed
